She criticized the BJP for allegedly vandalizing her residence and claimed their actions were politically motivated.  She also addressed concerns about voter suppression, highlighting the impact of voter deletion in certain constituencies. **Panja** emphasized the Trinamool Congress's focus on women-centric schemes like Lakshmi Bhandar, which aims to empower women financially. She also discussed the party's stance on issues such as crime against women and the lack of industry investment under the BJP government.

recent_articles.title: Assam Assembly election 2026: Curtains down on high-voltage campaign - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Assam Assembly elections concluded on April 7, with voters casting their ballots for the state's 126 seats. **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Home Minister Amit Shah**, and other BJP leaders campaigned against the opposition Congress, accusing it of promoting infiltrators and failing to address development issues. The Congress countered by highlighting corruption allegations against the ruling party and promising justice for singer Zubeen Garg if elected. Prominent candidates include Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, Gaurav Gogoi (Congress), Badruddin Ajmal (AIUDF), and Debabrata Saikia (opposition).  The elections will be held in a single phase on April 9th.

recent_articles.title: Assembly elections 2026: ECI may roll out SIR in remaining 17 States, 5 UTs post polls - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission** is considering rolling out the third and final phase of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) for voters' lists in 22 states and Union territories after the Assembly elections this month. The exercise, which aims to clean up electoral rolls, could begin after the polls conclude on April 29th or after the declaration of results.  The **Election Commission** has already conducted SIR in 10 states and three Union Territories, covering nearly 60 crore voters.

recent_articles.title: Once BJP comes to power in West Bengal, all infiltrators will be sent back: Amit Shah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, **Union Home Minister**, asserted that a change is inevitable in West Bengal and that all infiltrators from Assam, Tripura, and Bengal will be sent back to their countries if the BJP comes to power. He accused the **Congress** of supporting illegal immigrants and claimed that the party opposes the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) because it knows the law will prevent infiltrators from remaining in the state.  He also criticized the **Congress**, accusing them of building madrasas for Muslim students and calling the RSS and BJP snakes.

recent_articles.title: Names of people belonging to specific communities deleted from post-SIR voter rolls: West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, West Bengal Chief Minister, accused the state government of targeting specific communities in the deletion of names from voter rolls following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. She stated that **the Trinamool Congress (TMC)** will support those whose names were excluded and claimed that around 32 lakh names out of nearly 60 lakh cases under ‘adjudication’ had been restored after intervention in the Supreme Court.  The upcoming Assembly elections in West Bengal are scheduled for two phases on April 23 and 29, with counting taking place on May 4th.

recent_articles.title: Assam Police at Pawan Khera's residence in New Delhi; Himanta says Congress leader ‘ran away’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Assam** Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma** accused the **Congress** party of a “foreign-influenced misinformation campaign” against him and his wife, Riniki Bhuyan Sarma.  Following an investigation into allegations made by **Pawan Khera**, a **Congress** leader, about Ms. Sarma's alleged foreign assets, an **Assam** Police team is questioning **Khera** at his Delhi residence. The **Delhi** police are assisting in the proceedings.

recent_articles.title: Assam Assembly elections 2026: Bid to woo new voters in CM Himanta’s long-time constituency Jalukbari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the Chief Minister of Assam, filed his nomination papers for the upcoming Assembly elections in Jalukbari constituency.  He faces competition from **Bidisha Neog** of the Congress and **Dipika Das** of the Bhumi Adhikar Party. The delimitation exercise has shifted some areas within the constituency, but Sarma is expected to win with a comfortable margin. He has been actively campaigning in the area, focusing on development projects and community outreach.  The BJP is working hard to secure strong voter turnout in this region, particularly in Garigaon, where there has been significant improvement in infrastructure and social welfare schemes since the 2023 delimitation.

recent_articles.title: Assembly elections LIVE: Campaigning ends in Kerala, Assam, Puducherry today - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Public campaigning for the April 9 Kerala, Puducherry, and Assam Assembly polls ends on Tuesday. **Congress** in Kerala is ahead of its rivals, while **M.K. Stalin**, Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister and DMK president, claims the **Centre** has ignored Puducherry's plea for full statehood.  Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** urged voters to keep Congress out of power in Assam. The Election Commission of India (ECI) prohibits political advertisements from being published in newspapers on polling day or the day before.

recent_articles.title: Keep Congress away for peace, development: PM in Assam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** addressed election rallies in Assam, urging voters to keep the **Congress** party out of power for continued peace and development. He criticized the **Congress** for its alleged failure to address tribal poverty and violence, attributing it to their "bloody game" of politics and corruption.  Modi highlighted the NDA government's commitment to peace and development in the region, citing the example of the Bodos who suffered before the NDA's intervention. He also emphasized women's empowerment as a key priority for the BJP, highlighting its flagship Orunodoi scheme and the upcoming special session of Parliament on women's reservation.
